title: Remembering Live Aid
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant (with Jerry in the studio) look back at Live Aid, the July 1985 twin concerts at Wembley Stadium in London and JFK Stadium in Philadelphia. They cover the BBC/CBC reports on the 1984 Ethiopian famine that inspired Bob Geldof, the Band Aid single "Do They Know It's Christmas?", Harry Belafonte and Ken Kragen's USA for Africa and "We Are the World," and Boy George's push for a bigger concert. They describe the broadcast's scale (roughly 1.5 billion viewers, 160 countries, 13 satellites), the performers and memorable sets (Status Quo opening, Joan Baez, Bono and the dance during "Bad," Queen, Led Zeppelin with Phil Collins, Tom Petty, Bob Dylan, Mick Jagger and Tina Turner), artists who declined (Springsteen, Billy Joel, Michael Jackson, Huey Lewis, Van Halen), and the debate over where the money went in Ethiopia and Eritrea's civil war. The episode closes with a listener email about rape kits and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening banter and Live Aid memories
segments.summary: The hosts open with Jerry's memory of being in London during Live Aid, then discuss famous moments including Bono's dance during Bad, Pride in the Name of Love, and watching the concert footage on YouTube. They reminisce about watching it on MTV.

segments.title: Ethiopian famine documentary and Band Aid
segments.summary: The hosts describe how a BBC (or CBC) documentary on the Ethiopian famine, featuring a dying girl, moved Bob Geldof to organize Band Aid and the single 'Do They Know It's Christmas?', which raised over ten million dollars.

segments.title: USA for Africa and We Are the World
segments.summary: Harry Belafonte and Ken Kragen created the US response, USA for Africa, and the song 'We Are the World,' which Quincy Jones produced and Lionel Richie and Michael Jackson wrote. Boy George then suggested a bigger concert to Geldof.

segments.title: Planning and broadcast scale of Live Aid
segments.summary: Live Aid was organized in about six months, with concerts at Wembley in London and JFK Stadium in Philadelphia, linked by satellite to 160 countries and an estimated 1.5 billion viewers. The show opened with Status Quo and Joan Baez.

segments.title: Performances: Phil Collins, Queen, Led Zeppelin
segments.summary: Phil Collins played both continents. The hosts discuss Tom Petty's tight set, Queen's celebrated performance and its effect on donations, and Led Zeppelin's poor reunion set with Phil Collins on drums.

segments.title: Other performers, collaborations, and the Ethiopia money debate
segments.summary: The hosts cover Black Sabbath, Tom Petty, Bob Dylan, Mick Jagger and Tina Turner with Hall and Oates, and the closing We Are the World. They discuss artists who declined, including Billy Joel, Huey Lewis, Springsteen, and Michael Jackson, and debate whether money reached famine victims given Ethiopia's civil war and the government's role. The episode ends with a listener email and sign-off.
